title: Book Scene: What might an alien encounter look like? Tyson turns to science
byline: RACHEL FOWLER Special to the Yakima Herald-Republic
excerpt: With humor, science and plenty of pop culture references, Neil deGrasse Tyson’s latest book explores what we know — and don’t know — about possible alien life.
content:
Are we alone in the universe? Are aliens real? These are fascinating questions to ponder. Someone who has always been curious about this topic is the famous astrophysicist and author Neil deGrasse Tyson.

Aliens and possible encounters with them are the focus of his new book, “Take Me To Your Leader: Perspectives on Your First Alien Encounter.” Tyson is the author of many other books about the universe and astrophysics presented in an easy-to-understand way that makes the subjects much more approachable. My favorite of his is “Astrophysics for People in a Hurry.” His new book is a factual exploration of potential alien life mixed with fun pop culture references in film and literature.

The author breaks the book into a few different sections that explore what aliens might look like, how we would look to them, what their intelligence might be like, if they might have powers and how credible the evidence we currently have for them is. Tyson applies the scientific method, using the laws of physics, biology and chemistry to theorize answers.

Alongside the science, the author compares amusing depictions of aliens in well-known books, movies and shows like “Star Trek,” “Men in Black” and many others. He goes over what each one likely didn’t get right but shows how close others may have gotten. Throughout, Tyson maintains a close balance between what science tells us we could expect and what our imaginations have conjured.

The author himself notes that he has wanted to be abducted by aliens since he was a child, just so he could understand the universe better. His enthusiasm for space and science is palpable, while at the same time he is critical of the mostly blurry evidence we have for aliens from largely just a few countries.

In the author’s own words, he explains how you could view his book: “Think of Take Me To Your Leader as a book of etiquette and insights for your next close encounter, or perhaps a scientifically infused user’s manual with helpful hints from an astrophysicist who wants to meet the Aliens as badly as you do.”

While we get no hard evidence that an alien encounter will be soon, Tyson’s book is very fun and informative. He does an excellent job narrating the audiobook. His humor made me laugh, and his expertise in science, combined with his ability to make it understandable, kept me enthralled.

This is a tremendously enjoyable introduction to Tyson’s work if you haven’t read anything by him yet. The author dedicates the book to believers and skeptics alike, so I think whatever you believe, you’ll enjoy this book.

• Rachel Fowler is a bookseller at Inklings Bookshop. She and other Inklings staffers review books in this space every week.
